acceptance_criteria.condition: The Skill defines authoritative data ownership and lifecycle, stable error classes, retry/unknown handling, and privacy-safe diagnostics without forcing the same workflow on Level 0 work.
The Skill requires deliberate public-contract compatibility, migration and rollback, outcome/invariant-based tests, and deterministic treatment of time, randomness, concurrency, and external I/O.
The Skill requires measurable performance and resource budgets, low-cardinality actionable observability, and proportional trust-boundary review for applicable work.

Forward-test records show the combined rules applied to data deletion, public API performance evolution, and signed partner webhooks without treating unknown outcomes as success or creating speculative abstractions.

invariants: The Skill remains dependency-free and risk-scaled.
A public or cross-service change is not complete based only on a happy-path implementation.
Performance, availability, security, and privacy claims require measured or explicitly limited evidence.
AI-generated explanation is not a substitute for project facts, tests, traces, or independent review.

safeguards.name: failure and data contract
safeguards.rationale: The Skill requires ownership, lifecycle, error classes, retry/unknown policy, cancellation, and redacted diagnostics at applicable boundaries.

safeguards.name: contract and test discipline
safeguards.rationale: The Skill requires consumer-aware compatibility, migration/rollback, outcome/invariant tests, contract tests, and deterministic test inputs.

safeguards.name: operational and security readiness
safeguards.rationale: The Skill requires measured budgets, actionable low-cardinality telemetry, bounded work, and a proportional trust-boundary review.

safeguards.name: AI evidence discipline
safeguards.rationale: The Skill separates facts, hypotheses, and proposals; requires bounded changes, evidence, and adversarial independent review.

safeguards.name: structural and behavioral evaluation
safeguards.rationale: Standard-library contract tests retain the normative anchors while three independent forward tests exercise them in combined-risk maintenance scenarios.

design_boundary.rationale: The Skill owns its risk-scaled workflow while the validator owns the optional machine evidence representation.

dependency_audit.rationale: The package keeps evidence validation in the canonical root script and adds no dependency or reverse ownership edge.

extension_decision.rationale: The evidence schema extension is justified by a stable public machine-evidence contract and is covered by validator tests.

data_ownership.rationale: This package change does not create or mutate application business or personal data.

error_model.rationale: The Skill now requires stable failure classes and explicit retry and unknown-outcome decisions at applicable boundaries.

contract_evolution.rationale: The optional schema extension preserves validation compatibility for older artifacts while giving new artifacts an explicit quality-decision contract.

operational_budget.rationale: The Skill now requires measurable performance and resource budgets, plus actionable observability, for applicable work.

threat_boundary.rationale: The Skill now requires a proportional trust-boundary review for exposed or privileged behavior.

delivery_lifecycle.rationale: This earlier quality-policy change did not yet define commit, PR, release, or repository delivery workflow requirements.

release_recovery.rationale: This earlier quality-policy change did not alter a deployable service release or recovery plan.

data_migration.rationale: This earlier quality-policy change did not introduce a schema or data migration.

configuration_secrets.rationale: This earlier quality-policy change did not alter runtime configuration or secrets.

dependency_supply_chain.rationale: This earlier quality-policy change added no dependency or supply-chain control.

operational_knowledge.rationale: This earlier quality-policy change did not require an ADR or operator runbook.

reproducibility.rationale: This earlier quality-policy change did not alter project setup or environment reproduction guidance.

rollback_or_compatibility: Revert the Skill, README, generated agent metadata, validator, template, tests, captured evaluation artifacts, and this evidence artifact together. Existing project evidence remains compatible because quality_decisions and supporting_artifacts are optional schema extensions.

independent_review.notes: The initial review raised four issues. The follow-up review confirmed the backward-compatible schema, hash-verified support artifacts, complete final-report format, risk-scaled metadata, and regression tests; it required only this final replacement of pending/stale evidence records.

remaining_risks: The generic Skill cannot discover all real consumer contracts, data-retention laws, dependency cycles, SLO values, or threat models without project-specific evidence and tooling.
Forward tests demonstrate agent guidance in synthetic scenarios; they do not prove production integration, regulatory compliance, or hosted CI behavior.
